concepts.title: Electric Current, Potential Difference and Ohm's Law
concepts.body: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor, measured in amperes. One ampere equals one coulomb of charge passing per second. Potential difference between two points is the work done to move a unit charge from one point to the other, measured in volts. Ohm's law states that at constant temperature the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends. The constant of proportionality is the resistance R, so V = I R. A graph of V versus I for an ohmic conductor is a straight line through the origin.

concepts.title: Resistance, Resistivity and Combination of Resistors
concepts.body: Resistance of a conductor depends on its length L, cross-sectional area A, material nature and temperature. Resistivity ρ is the resistance of a unit cube of the material; R = ρ L / A. Resistivity changes with temperature but not with dimensions. In series combination the same current flows through all resistors and the equivalent resistance is the sum R_eq = R1 + R2 + ... . In parallel combination the potential difference across each resistor is the same and the reciprocal of equivalent resistance equals the sum of reciprocals 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... ; the equivalent resistance is always smaller than the smallest individual resistance. Series circuits are used where the same current is needed through all devices; parallel circuits are used in household wiring so each appliance receives the full supply voltage and operates independently.

concepts.title: Heating Effect of Current and Electric Power
concepts.body: When current passes through a resistor, electrical energy is converted into heat. The heat produced in time t is H = I² R t (Joule's law of heating). This effect is utilized in devices like electric heaters, toasters, incandescent bulbs and fuses. Electric power is the rate of energy consumption P = V I = I² R = V² / R. The commercial unit of electrical energy is kilowatt hour; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ joules. In a series circuit the current is not used up; it remains the same through all components. The resistance of a wire does not depend on the current flowing through it.

formulas.title: Ohm's Law and Resistance Formula
formulas.body: V = I R [V = volt, I = ampere, R = ohm]; R = ρ L / A [ρ = ohm metre, L = metre, A = square metre]. V is potential difference across the conductor, I is current through it, R is its resistance, ρ is resistivity of the material, L is length of the conductor, A is its cross-sectional area.

formulas.title: Power and Energy Relations
formulas.body: P = V I = I² R = V² / R [P = watt, V = volt, I = ampere, R = ohm]; E = P t [E = joule, P = watt, t = second]; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J. P is electric power, V is potential difference, I is current, R is resistance, E is energy consumed, t is time.

examples.title: Equivalent Resistance of Mixed Combination
examples.body: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected such that 3 Ω and 6 Ω are in parallel and this combination is in series with 2 Ω. Parallel part: 1/R_p = 1/3 + 1/6 = 2/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2, so R_p = 2 Ω. Total R_eq = 2 Ω + 2 Ω = 4 Ω. If a 12 V battery is connected, total current I = V/R_eq = 12/4 = 3 A. Voltage across parallel part = I × R_p = 3 × 2 = 6 V. Current through 3 Ω = 6/3 = 2 A, through 6 Ω = 6/6 = 1 A.

examples.title: Power and Energy Consumption of an Electric Heater
examples.body: An electric heater rated 1500 W, 220 V operates for 2 hours daily. Current drawn I = P/V = 1500/220 = 6.818 A. Resistance R = V²/P = 220²/1500 = 48400/1500 = 32.27 Ω. Energy consumed per day = 1.5 kW × 2 h = 3 kWh = 3 × 3.6 × 10⁶ = 1.08 × 10⁷ J. Monthly energy (30 days) = 90 kWh. Cost at ₹6 per kWh = 90 × 6 = ₹540.

mcqs.question: What is the SI unit of resistivity?
mcqs.explanation: Resistivity ρ = R A / L. Unit of R is ohm, A is m², L is m. So unit = ohm × m² / m = ohm metre.

mcqs.question: A 100 W, 200 V bulb is connected to a 160 V supply. What is the power consumed? (Assume resistance constant.)
mcqs.explanation: First find resistance at rated values: R = V²/P = 200²/100 = 40000/100 = 400 Ω. Then power at 160 V: P = V²/R = 160²/400 = 25600/400 = 64 W.

mcqs.question: Two resistors of 4 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel across a 6 V battery. What is the total current drawn from the battery?
mcqs.explanation: Equivalent resistance: 1/R_eq = 1/4 + 1/12 = 3/12 + 1/12 = 4/12 = 1/3, so R_eq = 3 Ω. Total current I = V/R_eq = 6/3 = 2 A.
